articles.description: Trump expects renewed U.S. bombing of Iran after the midterm elections, The Wall Street Journal reports, as Saudi-backed forces intercept projectiles.

articles.title: Apple faces $5.7 billion patent infringement verdict over iPhone and Apple Watch haptics
articles.description: A federal jury awarded Taction Technology more than $5.7 billion after finding Apple infringed claims from two haptics patents. Apple plans to appeal.

articles.title: Pennsylvania measles outbreak spreads, with 55 new cases reported since Wednesday
articles.description: 173 people hospitalized and four deaths in state so far, with less than 1% of those infected having been vaccinated The Pennsylvania department of health (DOH) announced on Friday that 55 new measles cases had been reported in the state since Wednesday, with officials continuing efforts to contain an outbreak of the disease that has spread across dozens of counties. In a news release , the DOH said that 890 measles cases had been confirmed across 39 counties in the state so far for the year. The outbreak had resulted in 173 hospitalizations in the state and four measles-associated deaths , the statement added.

articles.title: Power outages and flooded roads as major storm bears down on US north-east
articles.description: Thousands already without without power as New Jersey, Massachusetts, Delaware and New York brace for nor’easter More than 70,000 customers were without electricity in the north-eastern US on Saturday, a major sign of a powerful storm known as a nor’easter that was expected to create dangerous conditions through the weekend. Forecasters warned of gale winds that could down trees and heavy inundations that could flood roads.

articles.title: Supply glut, lab-grown alternatives: What's behind the fall of diamond prices to record lows
articles.description: Diamond prices are falling, leading investors and others to wonder whether the gemstones are losing their luster.

articles.title: New research finds 485 chemicals in US pesticide products linked to breast cancer
articles.description: Paper raises questions about safety of food and other products as early onset breast cancer rates surge worldwide New research has identified at least 485 chemicals used in US pesticide products that are linked to breast cancer, raising questions about the safety of food and other products at a time when early onset breast cancer rates are surging worldwide . The new peer-reviewed paper , published in Environmental Health Perspectives, a top journal from the American Chemical Society, highlights what public health advocates say are a range of deficiencies in how US pesticides are regulated. The review includes active pesticide ingredients, but also hundreds of so-called “inert”, or inactive, ingredients that typically do not undergo a thorough safety review.

articles.title: White House blocks CNN from Air Force One in latest escalation with news media
articles.description: Outlet had been scheduled to fly with Donald Trump to Tennessee for a college football game, network said Friday The White House has blocked CNN from traveling aboard Air Force One on Saturday, impeding its TV press pool duties in the latest escalation of the administration’s battle with the news media. CNN had been scheduled to fly with Donald Trump to Tennessee for a college football game, the network said on Friday . The White House confirmed CNN’s exclusion when it did not list the network on guidance sent to the press corps regarding Trump’s schedule for Saturday.

articles.title: Trump rejects Iran’s seven-day peace deal to reopen strait of Hormuz
articles.description: US president is said to expect renewed strikes after midterms US president Donald Trump has said he has rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the strait of Hormuz within a week and resume nuclear talks in return for the lifting of the US naval blockade of Iranian ports. “They made a proposal but I reject it,” he told reporters at the White House.

articles.title: Airlines waive change fees ahead of nor'easter as flight disruptions trickle in
articles.description: Flight disruptions were rising in Boston for Saturday.

articles.title: Angela Rayner stands by attack on care worker visa reforms ahead of Labour conference
articles.description: Housing secretary says Home Office moved goalposts with ‘disruptive’ change to permanent residence rules Angela Rayner has stood by her criticism of Home Office reforms that would make it harder for foreign care workers to claim permanent residence in the UK, describing them as “disruptive”. Last year, Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, announced that low paid migrants on jobs below graduate level would have to be in the country for 15 years before applying for settlement. Rayner previously attacked the plans as being “un-British” .

articles.title: Venezuelan shot by ICE in Austin needs surgery to avoid losing feeling in body, supporters say
articles.description: Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez has bullet lodged in back as accounts differ over events leading to traffic-stop shooting The Venezuelan man shot by federal immigration officers after a traffic stop in Texas needs surgery to avoid losing feeling on the left side of his body, according to his supporters. Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, 28, has spent the past five days in detention with a bullet lodged in his back, after Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) rapidly removed him from a hospital in Austin where he had been taken on Sunday after the shooting.

articles.title: Green shoots? Burnham cultivates rural links in attempt to ‘build back trust’ with farmers
articles.description: Ministers have been speaking to farming activists to try to build bridges after tax changes introduced under Starmer soured relations As an arable farmer, Olly Harrison’s WhatsApp messages are normally concerned with the more mundane matters of working the land: logistics, supplies and the occasional chat about the weather. So when a recent message came through from Andy Burnham, it was more than a little unexpected.

articles.title: UN adds 61 firms to settlements blacklist over alleged human rights violations against Palestinians
articles.description: Israel ‘categorically rejects’ publication and says businesses on database have committed no wrongdoing The UN human rights office has added 61 more companies to a blacklist of firms that it says are involved in violating Palestinian human rights through business ties to Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The vast majority of the total 214 companies, which are based in 11 countries, are Israeli. Five of the 158 companies listed last year were removed in the latest update.

articles.title: Work intensifying on UK laws to stamp out concert ticket touts, say sources
articles.description: Artists including Tinie Tempah and the Smiths’ drummer Mike Joyce ramp up pressure on government to keep its pledge to outlaw for-profit resales The government has stepped up work on new laws to stop ticket touts fleecing fans , as the prime minister came under pressure from artists including the drummer from the Smiths, one of his favourite bands. Keir Starmer said last year that the government would “stop fans from being ripped off” by outlawing the for-profit resale of tickets on sites such as Viagogo and StubHub, a pledge Labour first made in its 2024 election manifesto.

articles.title: We followed five people in Gaza from dawn to dusk – this is what the headlines don’t tell us
articles.description: Behind the stories of bombings and mass deaths, the everyday challenges facing Palestinians living under siege portray a quieter tragedy we rarely hear What does it take to make a morning cup of tea in Gaza? For Alaa Hessi , in her final month of pregnancy, this small ritual begins with a calculation of gas rations. Her family gets a ration of 6kg of gas every three months – enough to heat a pot for 18 precious minutes a day. That’s needed for cooking – so for tea, a fire must be built instead.

articles.title: Audemars Piguet says its Royal Pop collaboration with Swatch is breaking sales records, despite luxury watch slump and tariffs
articles.description: Swiss luxury watchmaker Audemars Piguet says its sales and engagement are breaking records after its risky, eye-catching Royal Pop collaboration with Swatch.

articles.title: Severely disabled young people should get fast-track access to benefits, Milburn says
articles.description: Alan Milburn said 16- to 24-year-olds with most complex needs should not have to keep proving they cannot work Young people whose complex disabilities mean they have little prospect of getting a paid job should get fast-track access to disability benefits, an official review of youth employment will say. The review, by the former Labour health secretary Alan Milburn, will say 16- to 24-year-olds with the most severe lifelong needs should be guaranteed swift and unconditional benefit support rather than having to prove they cannot work.

articles.title: Three-quarters of UK’s popular plug-in hybrid cars unable to use rapid chargers
articles.description: Only 26% of PHEVs sold across top 20 models can use chargers with power of 50kW or more, analysis finds Three-quarters of the 20 top-selling plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) in the UK cannot use rapid chargers, research has found, amid concerns that many are essentially “petrol cars pulling round a heavy battery”. The cars, which can run on electric batteries as well as combustion engines, have been promoted by carmakers as a way to cover long distances in a single drive – unlike fully electric cars – while still reducing emissions.

articles.title: Lula bans fixed-odds sports betting a week before Brazilian elections
articles.description: President’s ‘hard, drastic and necessary measure’, likely to attract widespread public support, polls suggest The Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has signed an order banning fixed-odds sports betting just over a week before the first round of the presidential election, in a move he said was designed to tackle the pervasive problem of families falling into debt. The decision ends the operation, offering, intermediation and advertising of betting.

articles.title: Drones could speed up getting defibrillators to people having cardiac arrests, study suggests
articles.description: New research suggests the technology could be used to increase out-of-hospital access to life-saving devices Drones could help cut the time it takes to get a defibrillator to people experiencing cardiac arrests when not in hospital, researchers have suggested. In the UK alone, there are more than 30,000 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests a year where emergency medical services attempt to resuscitate the individual, according to the British Heart Foundation. However, fewer than one in 10 people survive such an event, and some who do are left with neurological problems.

articles.title: British climber, 28, dies in fall in northern Spain
articles.description: Mountaineer’s body recovered about 20 metres below the summit of Torrecerredo, the highest peak of the Picos de Europa range A British man has died after falling about 61 metres (200ft) while descending from the summit of a mountain in northern Spain, according to local law enforcement. The 28-year-old mountaineer fell down a vertical gully on the east side of the Torrecerredo – the highest peak of the Cantabrian mountains – on Thursday afternoon, the Spanish Civil Guard for the Asturias region said.

articles.description: Province’s rat patrol called in to investigate as town of Bowden announces discovery of dead vermin For more than seven decades, residents of Alberta have shared something in common with Antarctica and the high Arctic: all locations are officially free of rats. But on Thursday the Canadian province’s reputation as a firewall against rodent infestation took a hit when the town of Bowden announced the discovery of a dead rat and called on the province’s “rat patrol” to investigate.

articles.title: Novelist accused of using AI to write book removed from French prize list
articles.description: Thélyson Orélien had been in the running to win a top literary prize before the AI claim emerged on social media The organisers of France’s most prestigious literary prize said they had removed a critically acclaimed novel by a Canadian-Haitian writer from the longlist after an anonymous online account claimed the book was “almost entirely” written by AI. The Académie Goncourt, a Paris-based literary organisation, said on Friday its decision to withdraw Thélyson Orélien’s novel C’était ça ou mourir (It Was That or Die) was “driven by the desire to preserve the integrity of the Goncourt prize and the academy itself, whose central role is to promote and honour literature written by women and men”.

articles.title: Pope Leo warns of AI threat to humanity at start of three-day France visit
articles.description: Pontiff says artificial intelligence must remain at service of people in first official papal visit to country in 18 years Pope Leo has warned against losing humanity in a “paradise of machines” as he addressed global concerns over the dangers of artificial intelligence at the start of a three-day visit to France. “If we are to avoid losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines invading and conditioning our daily lives, there is an urgent need for people to be educated in ethical discernment, capable of seeing what is morally right,” he said in a speech at the Élysée.

articles.title: Trump faces tough choices as Iran dangles deal to reopen Hormuz before US midterms
articles.description: Iran’s seven-day timetable would restart nuclear talks, but will the US be willing to deliver on terms that include reining in Israel in Lebanon? Iran’s seven-day timetable to reopen the strait of Hormuz and start talks on its nuclear programme has been pitched as a deal that could rapidly extricate Donald Trump from a political crisis but requires the US president to make difficult concessions. In the five days left before the proposed reopening of the strait, which is expected to relieve pressure on global energy markets, Trump would need to lift Iranian asset freezes, permit Iran to export its oil and, probably most difficult of all, order Benjamin Netanyahu to end Israel’s attacks on Hezbollah in Lebanon, thus achieving the “ceasefire on all fronts”.

He didn’t reveal the attack then, but he sounded a warning about the march of AI: “the risk is that AI develops in a way in which humans are no longer in control of what AI is producing.”

articles.description: Powered by sun and wind, the uncrewed vehicle will collect data to help Australian scientists better understand how oceans absorb emissions The seven-metre craft, which looks like a large kayak in hi-vis orange, is expected to travel about 22,000km through inhospitable waters, propelled by powerful westerly winds and energy from the sun. The journey is seven times the distance between Sydney and Perth.

articles.title: NSW crackdown on ‘AI-doctored’ real estate listings hits mural-covered wall
articles.description: Apartment with strange view singled out in government’s fight against deceptive ads – but real estate agent says photo is no fake Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast The New South Wales government’s crackdown on “AI-doctored” rental listings has hit a wall, after it made an example of a supposedly manipulated ad that turned out to be a genuine photograph of a $5,000 courtyard mural of Bondi beach. articles.title: Hurricane Polo barrels towards Baja California region of Mexico
articles.description: Area’s second-most intense hurricane on record being fuelled by exceptionally warm Pacific waters Hurricane Polo is barreling towards the Baja California region of Mexico, the latest system in a Pacific hurricane season that has been notably active in recent months. On 22 September, a measurement of 892 millibars was registered for Hurricane Polo, making it the second-most intense hurricane on record in the east Pacific. It is fuelled by exceptionally warm waters across the Pacific Ocean, providing favourable conditions for the system to maintain its considerable strength. Polo is expected to turn towards the west-north-west, before taking a more north-westerly trajectory on Saturday. It has maximum sustained winds of around 150mph, with even stronger gusts occurring within the most intense parts of the hurricane. Hurricane-force winds extend outward for approximately 40 miles from the centre, while tropical storm-force winds reach as far as 125 miles. These powerful winds, combined with torrential rainfall and dangerous seas, could have significant impacts. Although some fluctuations in intensity are possible over the coming days, Polo is expected to remain powerful as it tracks north-westwards.

articles.title: Pocock calls for AI safety act after Medicare breach – as it happened
articles.description: This blog is now closed Frontier AI now has capability to expose those vulnerabilities at a rate quicker than we can keep up, quicker than we can patch them. What if it was a less benign breach? What if it was a less benign actor? Let’s face it, clearly, Services Australia’s cybersecurity is woefully inadequate. I mean the irony here is that you actually need AI to fight AI. This should hasten, if anything, our move over in the US to less finger wagging and Trump one-upmanship, and more about embracing these AI companies and bringing them here so that we can have frontier models providing sovereign capability to Australia. Because AI is going to happen.

The former Yes musician, who has gone on to have a prolific solo career, played the piano at a Vietnamese bear sanctuary.

articles.title: Rebel offensive against Ethiopian army stokes fears of return to civil war
articles.description: Fighting escalates after Tigrayan rebels form new coalition aimed at overthrowing Abiy Ahmed government There are growing fears of a return to civil war in Ethiopia after an offensive by fighters from Tigray into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara and the formation of a new rebel alliance aimed at overthrowing the government of the prime minister, Abiy Ahmed. About 600,000 people died between 2020 and 2022 during a devastating war between the Ethiopian army and the political party and paramilitary group the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). Both sides are now accusing the other of triggering a return to open conflict.

articles.title: Backlash as Indian oil heir made professor of sustainability by Newcastle University
articles.description: Role for Anant Ambani, son of India’s richest person, who also runs a controversial mega-zoo, met with incredulity Newcastle University is facing a backlash from conservationists over the appointment of the heir to an Indian oil and gas fortune who runs a controversial mega-zoo as a professor of sustainability. The university announced that Anant Ambani had been given a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship” and “significant contributions to advancing a more sustainable future”.

articles.title: 特朗普為何親赴機場，超規格接待習近平？
articles.description: 這是習近平時隔11年再次國事訪問美國。更是相隔64年，再有美國總統親自迎接他國元首到訪。有學者向BBC中文分析特朗普的舉動，既是在與中方「做生意打交道」；也是在向美國民眾展示自己的能力。

articles.title: Alarm bells sound in Brussels as EU sales of Chinese hybrid cars rocket
articles.description: Explosive growth in imported vehicles omitted from EV tariffs fuels concern for future of European carmakers EU imports three times more from China than bloc exports there Sales of Chinese hybrid cars have rocketed in the EU in the past four and a half years, data shows, underlining growing concerns in Brussels over the future of the European car industry. In 2022, just 659 Chinese-made fully hybrid cars (vehicles in which the petrol or diesel engine charge the motor and battery) were sold in the EU. However, after Brussels imposed anti-subsidy tariffs on fully electric cars from China in 2024, sales of hybrids have shot up to 160,662 in the first seven months of this year.

articles.title: 習近平訪美首日看點：誰同行？第一夫人角色？高規格接待引反彈？
articles.description: BBC中文整理，習近平抵達華盛頓一刻，外界關注的重點看點：誰是習近平訪美團成員？美國共和黨及人民對中國的態度為何？

articles.title: OpenAI智能體入侵澳洲政府網站竊取資料 官方兩月後才發覺
articles.description: OpenAI在事發後兩個月才察覺事件，並遲至本月中，才用一般電郵的方式通知澳洲政府。澳洲政府形容事件令人震驚，批評OpenAI的處理手法「不可接受」。

articles.title: France's fresh budget battle threatens to topple another government
articles.description: Time is not on the side of French government bonds, strategists have warned, as the nation's deficit balloons.

articles.title: World heads into food crises 'blind' as U.S. aid cuts squeeze UN food agency, experts warn
articles.description: Climate shocks, conflict and a global fuel crisis, on top of surging interest rates and donor cuts, leave agencies less able to help those facing higher food prices.

articles.title: 俄羅斯佔領烏克蘭城市：居民靠野菜維生，死者遺體「棄置街頭」
articles.description: BBC採訪了遭俄羅斯佔領的烏克蘭城鎮奧列什基居民，他們表示自己正「持續不斷遭受炮擊」。

articles.title: 習近平開展訪美 貝森特宣佈兩國貿易戰繼續「停火」
articles.description: 中國國家主席習近平專機抵達首都華盛頓附近的安德魯斯聯合基地，美國總統特朗普（川普）打破慣例，親自接機。

articles.title: 習近平訪美晤特朗普：中美AI超級強國的雄心成為焦點
articles.description: 美國與中國正爭奪人工智能領先地位，同時尋求確保這項技術仍在人類掌控之中。

articles.title: 中國希望伊朗戰爭結束，但不是以特朗普想要的方式
articles.description: 分析人士指，北京可能推動德黑蘭重啟談判，但不太可能停止購買伊朗石油。

articles.title: 「你有五年規劃，我有移民計劃」：香港年輕人為何焦慮？
articles.description: 9月16日，香港特首李家超發表香港首個五年規劃文件及年度施政報告。但在網絡上，部分年輕人卻開始討論如何離開香港。BBC中文訪問三位香港青年，了解他們的看法。

articles.title: 草原上的數據中心：中國AI雄心背後的算力前線
articles.description: 在中國內蒙古遼闊的草原上，數十座數據中心正以驚人速度拔地而起。曾經的農田與草原，正在快速轉變為支撐中國AI雄心的「引擎」，以滿足狂飆的算力需求。

articles.title: 習特會前瞻：特朗普會再度爭取「釋放黎智英」嗎？
articles.description: 中美兩國元首即將會面，有學者分析，特朗普將在會面期間提及黎智英案，中方釋放黎智英是展現中國軟實力的合適時機，但相信機率不大。

articles.title: Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in years
articles.description: Sunil Bharti Mittal’s Airtel Money targets $9bn IPO in boost for ailing UK stock market Nils Pratley: Does this mark the end of London’s listing drought? Not yet A payments business that operates across Africa and is ultimately controlled by an Indian billionaire has announced its intention to float on the struggling London Stock Exchange . Airtel Money, the mobile money arm of Airtel Africa, is planning one of the biggest UK listings in years, in a boost for the shrinking London market that has faced a string of recent departures .

articles.title: Top South African police officer charged with raping woman, 18, and grooming 16-year-old girl
articles.description: Arrest of Shadrack Sibiya comes as country reels from cases of femicide and alleged police corruption and criminality One of South Africa’s most senior police officers has been charged with raping an 18-year-old woman and grooming a 16-year-old girl, as the country’s police face allegations of corruption and failing to tackle violence against women and girls. Shadrack Sibiya, who was already suspended from his role as deputy national police commissioner over allegations he interfered with political killings investigations, was arrested on Monday. He is facing charges of rape, people trafficking, promoting the sexual grooming of a child and two counts of grooming a child.

articles.title: 特朗普與習近平會面在即，中國的AI雄心正在烏蘭察布高歌猛進
articles.description: BBC探訪內蒙古，一名工人表示，北京的AI基礎設施正以「中國速度」推進。

articles.title: 日本以街道整潔無瑕而聞名，但為什麼公共垃圾桶卻如此難找？
articles.description: 如果你花一天時間在東京觀光，可能會發現自己一路拿著空咖啡杯、7-Eleven蛋三明治的包裝紙，以及愈來愈強烈的困惑感。日本以重視整潔聞名，那麼，為什麼卻找不到地方丟垃圾呢？

articles.title: 香港提出「人民幣支付政府開支」為何引發「去美元化」憂慮？
articles.description: 有經濟學者對BBC中文指出，港府希望建立「示範作用」，未來甚至「可能連收稅都收人民幣」，增加其他國家在香港使用人民幣買賣黃金、投資股票的信心。

articles.title: Sri Lanka Easter bombings: 15 sentenced to hundreds of years in prison each over deadly terror attacks
articles.description: Islamic State-inspired bombings of churches and hotels in 2019 was one of the country’s worst ever attacks A court in Sri Lanka has convicted 15 men on terrorist charges for their involvement in the deadly 2019 Easter bombings and sentenced them each to at least 220 years in prison. The terror attacks, which targeted luxury hotels and churches as they held Easter services, left 267 people dead and wounded almost 600. The bombings, which were inspired by Islamic State (IS), were among the deadliest terror attacks in Sri Lanka’s history and sent shockwaves through the country.

articles.title: 外星生命會讓我們生病嗎？太空微生物帶來哪些風險
articles.description: 數十年來，我們一直在尋找地球以外的生命。然而，如果我們發現的是微生物，就必須確保它們不會令我們染病。

articles.title: 從年輕縣官到國家主席：習近平41年來的訪美影像
articles.description: 習近平即將到訪美國會晤特朗普（川普），這將是他歷來第11次以中國官方身份訪美。從31歲縣委書記到中國國家主席，BBC中文透過歷年照片，回顧他的訪美行程如何隨身份和中美關係變化。

articles.title: 「雙休購」爆紅與下架：一個網購平台如何撬動勞工權益討論
articles.description: 提倡雙休的民間自發平台「雙休購」曇花一現後快速被下架，中國打工人開始在社交媒體上要求雙休正當權利。學者指這樣的消費抵制是正向的發展。

articles.title: ‘What we have is unique’: the Indian craftsmanship behind global luxury fashion
articles.description: Generations of artisans from Mumbai to Lucknow have shaped the world’s most coveted designs. Plus, the gen Z memes giving classic Bollywood a new life The zardozi embroidery on a Dior dress, the T-strap leather sandals at a Prada show, the mirror-work technique used on a Fendi bag – for decades, the skill of Indian artisans has been an invisible force behind some of the world’s most coveted fashion. Now, that work is beginning to claim its own place in the spotlight, and the Mumbai-based textile and embroidery atelier Chanakya International is at the forefront.

articles.title: Healthcare in Africa ‘under growing strain’ after US withdrawal from aid programs, report warns
articles.description: Accra Reset’s report states countries in the region and global south should take greater control of their health development after USAID debacle The United States’ withdrawal from key aid programs has put healthcare in Africa and the global south “under growing strain” a new report warns. The report says the Trump administration’s cuts to programs such as US Agency for International Development (USAID), as well as the Covid-19 pandemic and rising costs of living globally have brought “new urgency” for the need to reform healthcare in the region.

articles.title: Pakistan jails sisters of Imran Khan before protest seeking his release
articles.description: Police crack down on family and political supporters of former PM who say authorities are ‘slowly killing’ him in prison Three sisters of Pakistan’s incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan have been arrested amid a heavy-handed government crackdown on plans for a nationwide protest to demand Khan’s release. The lawyer for the three sisters, Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, said on Monday that they had all been detained and jailed for 30 days under a warrant that accused them of being a threat to public order.

articles.title: 戴安娜弟弟出書談王室 查爾斯曾稱她「很快會被遺忘」
articles.description: 戴安娜王妃逝世近30年之際，她的弟弟史賓賽伯爵出版新書，重提姐姐去世後的王室事件。他聲稱，時任王儲查爾斯曾認為戴安娜很快會被世人遺忘，但這項說法遭到王室否認。

articles.title: Banished to alien lands: Trump’s secret deportation deals
articles.description: After a plane journey in shackles, an Iranian woman found herself in the middle of Africa in a country she did not know existed. She is one of thousands deported from the US on the back of shadowy deals made with dozens of countries. An in-depth investigation reveals the ‘show of force’ costing American taxpayers millions No one would tell the shackled detainees onboard the US immigration plane where they were going. The officers in charge would taunt them when they asked, they said. It was only when the seat-back video screens finally showed a map that the 18 migrants worked it out.

articles.title: 領英高層分享6個人脈竅門，幫你更快找到工作
articles.description: 從咖啡閒聊到領英訊息，以下是如何透過人脈關係找到下一份工作的方法。

articles.title: 美中峰會前，蕭美琴訪歐背後的「利基」外交
articles.description: 但在這樣的空間中，仍浮現出一條外交路徑：交往對象既不是一個主權國家，而是一個國際組織（即歐盟）；同時也不是其行政分支，而是其立法分支（歐洲議會）。這一雙重錯位，可以找到一個不容易受到中國壓力的外交場域。

articles.title: 2026台灣地方選舉：「九合一」為何重要？選舉時程是什麼？
articles.description: 台灣的地方選舉又稱「九合一」選舉，每四年一次，多數落在總統任期中段的年底，故被視為總統的「期中考」。

articles.title: 「我接受了11年化療，卻發現從未患癌」
articles.description: 貝姬·瓊斯（Becky Jones）21歲被告知患有末期腦癌，接受了長達11年的化療，近期才發現根本不是癌症。和她有類似經歷的，還有同一間醫院的另外40多名病患。

articles.title: 星宇股份解約風波：107名應屆生「告洋狀」揭示中國勞工維權現狀
articles.description: 9月9日，就近期在中國引起轟動的「星宇股份解約107位應屆生」事件，上交所向星宇股份下發監管工作函，港交所延緩其上市審核，此前，公司董事長周曉萍已公開道歉。

articles.title: 俄烏戰場為何或會迎來新一批朝鮮軍人
articles.description: 朝鮮（北韓）士兵於2024年底被平壤派遣，與俄羅斯部隊並肩作戰，試圖擊退烏克蘭的一次攻勢。烏克蘭總統澤連斯基表示，俄羅斯沃羅涅日地區正進行準備，以接收新一批朝鮮部隊。

articles.title: 協助死亡：世界各地法律有何不同
articles.description: 全球約有4億人可以獲得某種形式的協助死亡（安樂死）服務，這些國家的政策都是怎樣的？

articles.title: 人工智能踩「剎車」？特朗普：別忘了中美競爭
articles.description: 上星期六，達里奧·阿摩迪（Dario Amodei）呼籲放緩發展步伐,以「降低出現嚴重問題的風險」，奧特曼和馬斯克均表示認同。這名Anthropic行政總裁同時強調，任何放緩都必須有所限度，以免讓中國反超領先。

articles.title: 中國強勢下，歐洲電池工業謀求「重新充電」
articles.description: 歐洲擁有一些前景可期的電池技術，但它能否追回被中國電池巨頭拉開的差距？

articles.title: 專家評中國修《國防動員法》：吸俄烏教訓實現「平戰快速轉換」
articles.description: 新法還首次明定，18至60歲男性、18至55歲女性原則上須擔負國防勤務；金融、交通、電信、能源、醫療、糧食等關鍵領域，在動員期間均可採取特別措施。

articles.title: 習近平七年再訪印度：金磚峰會握手背後，中印關係破冰？
articles.description: 金磚峰會《新德里宣言》呼籲對伊朗戰爭「最大克制」卻不點名美國。而習近平七年首訪印度，中印關係解凍了嗎？

articles.title: 女性比男性更擅長耐力跑嗎？
articles.description: 近月來，女性在多項備受矚目的耐力賽事中擊敗男性對手。她們是否天生更適合這類挑戰？

articles.title: 香港支聯會「煽動顛覆」案：被告們的伴侶與戰友
articles.description: 香港支聯會「煽顛」案歷經五年，三名核心人物的判刑結果塵埃落定。BBC中文訪問李卓人的妻子鄧燕娥及鄒幸彤戰友劉家儀，講述他們如何面對香港的變遷和怎樣陪伴在牆內的人。

articles.title: 美軍航母全數撤離印太：台灣該擔心「空窗期」嗎？
articles.description: 專家稱，航母給美國盟友的是心理保證。印太區域沒有航母，「會加強一種整體感覺：美國正被中東局勢分心。」
